messages:
tyler-cs: Heads up — several customers reporting p95/p99 regressions on tool-calling endpoints starting ~11:00 UTC. They say tool routing + JSON schema validation adds noticeable latency.

jamie-support: saw multiple tickets. Cust A included traces: p95 climbed from ~220ms to ~600ms and p99 to ~3.4s around 10:58 UTC.

ivan-runtime: can you paste a sanitized trace? need to know which steps spike — parsing, validation, dispatch? any model or runtime changes?

tyler-cs: pasted sanitized trace from Cust A: 
```
request_id=rcpt_01XXZ
route=tool_router
steps=[parse_prompt:12ms, select_tool:8ms, validate_schema:180ms, dispatch_tool:240ms, assemble_response:30ms]
total=470ms (p95)
```
validate_schema + dispatch_tool look large.

megan-sre: did infra do anything around 11:00? autoscaler events, node churn?

build-bot: no user-facing deploys 09:30-12:00 UTC. autoscale: scale-up for pool-gpu-2 at 10:52, no failures recorded.

ivan-runtime: hypothesis: validators are being compiled per-request (AJV compile+run). We should cache compiled validators by schema_id; current router runs sync validation before enqueue, blocking request path.

lindsey-eng: recall we flipped strict JSON coercion on by default in last runtime patch (rolled 3 days ago). That can add overhead for complex schemas, especially if we recompile.

jamie-support: affected customers: cust_A (org_77), cust_B (org_101), cust_C (org_215). All using function/tool calling with structured_output + custom schemas.

ivan-runtime: immediate mitigations: 
- enable schema-compiler cache (compile-on-first-use, reuse validator instance)
- run validation async (optimistic accept, validate in background)
- fast-path skip for no-schema or tiny schemas
- offload dispatch from main request thread (enqueue early)

megan-sre: is FLAG_SCHEMA_CACHE available to flip?

lindsey-eng: yes FLAG_SCHEMA_CACHE exists but default off. We can flip per-region. Risk: memory growth if we cache many tenant schemas.

ivan-runtime: use an LRU with size cap (e.g., 500 entries) and compile-time limit to mitigate memory/compile stalls. We can flip the flag for immediate perf gains.

tyler-cs: customers asking ETA — can we do a hotfix in ~2h?

ivan-runtime: plan: small hotfix enabling FLAG_SCHEMA_CACHE in EU/US, cache size 500, compile-time cap 50ms. Also change router to enqueue before heavy validation and add streaming indicator. I'll prepare a canary.

deploy-bot: rolling canary: runtime-service v3.4.7-hotfix-schema-cache -> canary-id cny_115 (3 nodes).

lindsey-eng: adding telemetry: instrument validate_schema duration, tool_dispatch wait + dispatch durations; add tags org_id, schema_id, tool_id.

jamie-support: I'll contact affected customers with a heads-up and request a test call when canary completes. Also collecting sample request bodies for repro.

tyler-cs: repro steps (from Cust A):
1) curl POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat?mode=tools -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" -d '{"model":"rwd-llm-3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"..."}],"tools":[{"name":"invoice_extractor","schema_id":"sch_998"}],"stream":false}'
2) check X-Redwood-P95 header or trace link
3) attach full response headers + route trace

ivan-runtime: I'll run local load with their schema and measure compile/validate times.

megan-sre: monitoring: create temporary alert if validate_schema p95 > 200ms OR tool_dispatch p95 > 300ms, scoped to orgs >1k req/day to lower noise.

ivan-runtime: quick micro-opts: precompile validators at startup for top schemas; avoid defensive deep clones before validation; consider fast-json-stringify for shaping outputs where relevant.

lindsey-eng: note: fast-json-stringify helps serialization; for validation AJV compile + validateSync is best. Ensure compiled validators are reused and thread-safe.

tyler-cs: customers also seeing p99 spikes; fallback to keep UI usable?

ivan-runtime: fallback options: 
- policy to skip strict validation if validate_schema > 200ms and mark X-Redwood-Validation:skipped + async validation job + audit log
- lightweight_tool_router feature that accepts string payloads and bypasses structured-output enforcement

jamie-support: customers will accept skipped validation if notified and provided async audit results.

megan-sre: recommend gradual rollout: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with metric gates.

ivan-runtime: timeline: 0-30m flip FLAG_SCHEMA_CACHE in canary and add spans; 30-90m monitor canary; 90-180m ramp if good. PR for async-validate + streaming created.

deploy-bot: canary complete on 3 nodes. metric snapshot: validate_schema p95 reduced 420ms -> 90ms for canary traffic. tool_dispatch unchanged.

ivan-runtime: promising. opening PR for async-validate & stream: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/4823. Assigning reviewers @lindsey-eng @megan-sre.

lindsey-eng: review incoming. ensure audit logs for skipped validations for compliance customers.

tyler-cs: customer-facing note draft: \"We've identified schema validation as the main source of recent latency on tool-calls. We're rolling a hotfix that caches compiled validators and enabling an opt-in lightweight routing mode. We'll monitor and follow up with timelines.\"

jamie-support: sending that to affected customers and asking for test calls. Linking tickets: TKT-3245 (cust_A), TKT-3247 (cust_B), TKT-3251 (cust_C).

megan-sre: postmortem checklist if rollout regresses: revert flag, reduce cache size, collect heap profiles, ensure OOM/GC alerts.

ivan-runtime: updating incident doc with repro, telemetry queries, PR link, mitigation steps.

tyler-cs: thanks all — keep updates here. If anyone sees p99 > 2s for top orgs ping me with trace.

inc-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1342 (latency: tool-calling schema validation). Severity: Sev3. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/INC-2026-1342

jamie-support: added ticket refs in support system.
